blogs.title: When It Comes Back Again — TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV After Endocarditis
blogs.description: This post dives into the complex clinical decision‐making that underpins a third transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) after treated prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE). It contrasts current ESC 2025 guidelines advocating surgery for PVE against real-world scenarios where surgical options are prohibitive because of frailty or prior infections. By dissecting patient‐specific risk factors—EuroSCORE II, CAD burden, prior infections—and weighing them against durable valve performance data from serial TAVR studies, clinicians gain insight into when repeat TAVR is justified.

blogs.title: Sculpting Success — CT‑Guided Planning For Triple Transcatheter Valves
blogs.description: The bedrock of any repeat valve‐in‐valve procedure is meticulous imaging workup – especially when three prosthetic layers are stacked together. This article outlines step-by-step CT evaluation protocols used in the TAV‑in‑TAV‑in‑TAV case—measuring annulus dimensions, assessing effective landing zones, visualising previous stents’ geometry and estimating valve‑to‑coronary distances. It also highlights emerging software tools that allow virtual deployment simulations and three-dimensional modelling along with specific pitfalls such as overlapping frame artefacts that can mislead sizing.

blogs.title: High Above the Slope — Implant Depth To Prevent Coronary Obstruction And Boost EOAr
blogs.description: A central technical nuance illustrated by this case is intentional ‘high implantation’ of the nova Acurate Neo 2 over previously deployed Evolut leaflets. This section explains why positioning at the level of older leaflets preserves downstream lumen space—but only if supported by precise CT chalking and fluoroscopic landmarks for commissural alignment. Readers will learn how this manoeuvre reduced neo‐skirt formation below the coronary ostia while preventing patient–prosthesis mismatch by maximizing post‐dilatation geometry.

blogs.title: Keeping the Door Open — Preserving Coronary Access After Multiple Stent Valves
blogs.description: In patients who may need future coronary interventions after repetitive transcatheter replacements, maintaining accessible coronary ostia is paramount. This piece reviews strategies—from placing valves with sympathetic commissural alignment toward native sinus orientation to proactively guiding distal wire passage during initial deployment—that mitigate obturation risks introduced by successive stainless steel stent frames.

blogs.title: Preventing Prosthesis–Patient Mismatch Through Valve Selection & Deployment Strategy
blogs.description: Despite a third valved device utilizing an expandable snare concept often leads to elevated gradients immediately post‐deployment—as seen here—the challenge lies in achieving durable results without severe prosthesis–patient mismatch (PPM). This post outlines best practices in selecting self-expandable versus balloon-expandable valves based on annular size and previous frame architecture together with proactive moulding via post-dilatation balloons that smooth out stent–leaflet interfaces.

blogs.title: Beyond The Benchmarks — One Year Follow-Up After Multi-Valve Intervention
blogs.description: Serial hemodynamic metrics reveal how initial high gradients resolve over time following successful de facto valve restoration—even while residual moderate stenosis remains nominally present at one year post-procedure. This article synthesises longitudinal echo data—from immediate post-procedural peaks through month four improvements—to demonstrate how early left ventricular reverse remodeling translates into symptomatic reassessment and durable functional status when serial valve degeneration occurs.
